summary: Children are guaranteed two thirds of the estate, up to a cap per child, and a will cannot reduce it. Norway has no trust law and is outside the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations exist but family foundations are restricted.
reserved_share: Descendants: 2/3 of the estate, capped at 15 times the National Insurance basic amount (about NOK 1.8 million in 2025) per child; Inheritance Act 2019. Article number not confirmed; spouse's minimum share not checked.
foreign_law_note: Norway is not an EU state and the Succession Regulation does not apply; its own conflict rules were not confirmed for foreigners choosing their national law.
trust_note: No trust law; foreign trusts are not recognised by treaty and tax treatment was not checked. Foundations Act 2001 permits foundations, with limits on benefit to the founder's family.
open_questions: Article numbers for the forced share and current cap.
Choice of law for foreign residents.
Tax on foreign trusts and family foundations.
